headline: Scalable tools and catalogues for pathogen genomes, mobile elements and viral variation
label: Microbial Pathogen Genome Analysis
summary: Offline nanopore diagnostics, alignment-free viral variant calling and planetary-scale MGE and prophage resources broaden practical microbial genome analysis.
synthesis: The dominant thread is infrastructure for characterizing pathogen and microbial genome content, spanning read-level methods, workflows and large catalogues. On the read side, EMtrace runs nanopore metagenomics offline on a laptop, combining read classification, EM-based abundance estimation and consensus genome assembly. bronko detects viral SNPs, indels and minor variants directly from reads without alignment, with near-linear scaling in depth. Accessory-genome resources include proMGE2, cataloguing over 16.4 million mobile genetic elements from isolates and MAGs, and PHI, a Galaxy workflow for prophage identification, host prediction and standardized reporting. gcPathogen 2.0 expands a multi-omics pathogen surveillance database. Two items analyze genome structure directly: NMF decomposition of 1,398 S. aureus genomes yields 24 additive accessory modules separating lineage from adaptation and virulence, and an optimized PacBio HiFi strategy produces near-complete genomes of Malian P. falciparum field isolates, resolving telomeric regions.
